EXECUTED ANALYSIS COMPLETE.

HEADLINE ANSWER: The interaction effect between BCG vaccination status and prior medical history on COVID-19 severity is not statistically detectable. In the primary ordinal logistic model (subject-level max AESEV over RTI-category AEs, levels 1<2<3<4; n=529 complete cases), the interaction odds ratio — the ratio of the BCG-vs-Placebo severity OR among subjects with prior medical history to that among subjects without — is OR = 0.80 (95% CI 0.39–1.64, p = 0.55). Stratum-specific BCG effects: OR 1.35 (0.88–2.08) without prior history and OR 1.09 (0.61–1.93) with prior history. Prior medical history itself is associated with higher severity (OR ≈ 2.0, p ≈ 0.01), but it does not modify the BCG effect in this analysis.

ANALYTIC SAMPLE (primary, complete-case on RTI outcome): 529 of 1,000 subjects analyzed. Exclusions (no RTI-category AE or all severity missing) by stratum: BCG/priorhx=0: 168/343 (49.0%); BCG/priorhx=1: 56/157 (35.7%); Placebo/priorhx=0: 187/348 (53.7%); Placebo/priorhx=1: 60/152 (39.5%) — mildly differential (prior-history subjects more likely retained), which is why sensitivity (c) re-includes them. Analytic cell sizes: BCG/priorhx=0: 175, BCG/priorhx=1: 101, Placebo/priorhx=0: 161, Placebo/priorhx=1: 92. Outcome distribution: 253/253/16/7 at levels 1/2/3/4.

SENSITIVITY TABLE (interaction OR, same spec):
- PRIMARY: max AESEV over RTI AEs, complete-case (n=529): 0.804 (0.394–1.641), p=0.55
- (a) max AESEV over ALL AEs (n=529): 0.793 (0.387–1.623), p=0.53
- (b) max AESEV over COVID-19-labeled AEs (n=150): 0.917 (0.245–3.434), p=0.90
- (c) no-RTI-AE subjects assigned lowest category (n=954): 0.823 (0.456–1.484), p=0.52
- (d) priorhx including "Other:" free-text conditions (n=529): 1.502 (0.733–3.078), p=0.27
- (d+c) combined (n=954): 1.198 (0.656–2.189), p=0.56

STABILITY READING: The interaction OR is stable (0.79–0.92, always non-significant) across all outcome definitions and missing-data handling with the 14-item core comorbidity definition of prior history. It reverses direction (1.20–1.50, still non-significant) only when "Other:" free-text conditions are folded into priorhx — i.e., the point estimate is definition-dependent but in no specification is there a significant interaction; all CIs comfortably include 1.0. The defensible conclusion is "no evidence of an interaction" rather than any specific direction or magnitude.

MODEL DETAILS (primary): statsmodels OrderedModel, logistic cumulative link; covariates: bcg, priorhx, bcg×priorhx, patients_seen (categorical: 51-100 OR 0.89 p=0.65; >100 OR 1.66 p=0.34, ref 1-50), age band (ref <30), SEX (2 vs 1), work_hours (41-80+ vs 1-40, >80 pooled). Cut-point constants: 1/2 OR 1.60, 2/3 OR 3.26, 3/4 OR 1.23. Proportional-odds informal check: binary logit P(Y>=2) gives interaction OR 0.72 (p=0.37), direction consistent with the ordinal model; cuts Y>=3 and Y>=4 are unusable due to complete separation (only 23 subjects at levels 3-4) — a limitation inherent to the sparse upper tail.

LIMITATIONS: (1) severity labels 1–4 are inferred (mild→life-threatening) from AESER/Fatal cross-validation, not documented in the data; (2) ~47–53% of subjects excluded in the primary complete-case analysis because RTI events carry no AESEV, mildly differential by stratum; sensitivity (c) mitigates this; (3) only 7 subjects at severity level 4 and 16 at level 3 limit power for high-severity contrasts; (4) patients_seen is banded, not exact; (5) the "Other:" definition sensitivity shows the priorhx composite is not uniquely determined by the data.
